newsitem.title: ITALY: Algerian opposition leader urges U.S. action.
newsitem.headline: Algerian opposition leader urges U.S. action.

text.p: Algeria's main secular opposition leader, Hocine Ait Ahmed, called on U.S. President Bill Clinton on Thursday to appoint a special mediator to help end the spiral of violence in the North African country.

Speaking to journalists in Rome, he said Algeria was lurching towards all-out chaos and blamed France, which has close links with the military-backed government, of prime responsibility for international inaction on the crisis.

"One of the initiatives we expect is that President Clinton takes a measure likely to help bring about peace. Why doesn't he appoint a mediator on Algeria?" asked Ait Ahmed, leader of the Socialist Forces Front (FFS).
"We believe that such an initiative in favour of a peace process is likely to unblock the situation, the international situation," he said.

Algerian newspapers on Thursday said nearly two weeks of bombings by Islamist guerrillas had killed at least 160 people, the latest deaths in five years of violence since authorities cancelled a general election that Islamists were poised to win.

News reports speak of 60,000 deaths but Ait Ahmed put the toll at 100,000 and accused President Liamine Zeroual of using the emergency to suppress democracy. "The current debate is either war or peace. The rest is secondary," he said.
